record_type_quote: Therapists and friends often encourage people to say how they feel (ie. name their emotions) in order to help them cope, however previous research demonstrates that naming one's emotions prior to regulating makes it harder to regulate (Nook et al., 2021). We aimed to replicate and extend this finding to determine how the relationship between naming and emotion regulation changes across the lifespan.

targets.outcome_quote: Our study examined two age groups, younger adults (18, 25, N=37) and older adults (60+, N=44), using a mixed design and found that naming emotions prior to regulation impeded regulation in both groups, but more so in the older adult group.
